name: Tim Dooley Atlas — Unified Manifest
purpose: The canonical map of the repository. Internal datasets remain modular, but the atlas presents them as one system with stable layers, routes, record identity, relationships and evidence.
principle: One atlas, many layers. Records are the objects; relationships explain how they connect; evidence explains what is known; architecture explains where things belong.

architecture.rule: The architecture is a project-defined interpretive frame; it does not convert metaphor into empirical evidence.

architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.purpose: Canonical Frame, Tree and 33-level information architecture.

graph.label: Graph
graph.purpose: Canonical records and explicit relationships joining the archive.

world.label: World
world.purpose: The canonical 195-nation world layer and its geographic, institutional and social enrichment.

research.label: Evidence
research.purpose: Facts, sources, events and research material with provenance and confidence.

systems.label: Systems
systems.purpose: Economic, energy, infrastructure, technology, labour, finance and strategic-system studies.

mythology.label: Potatoism
mythology.purpose: Project mythology, symbols, lore and interpretive architecture, kept distinct from empirical evidence.

count_definitions.core_atlas_records: nodes + tree-child records + tree-support records; this is a navigational core, not a repository file count.
count_definitions.sources: source records referenced by research/event/country evidence layers.
count_definitions.enriched_nations: canonical nations with active enrichment overlays according to data/country-layer-manifest.json.

compatibility.status: backend.json remains the machine health/endpoint registry; atlas-manifest.json is the human-facing canonical map.

retirement_policy: Do not delete a legacy dataset merely because another layer overlaps it. First establish a canonical owner, migrate consumers, mark the old file as compatibility-only, then remove it only when no live route depends on it.
rule: Never require the user to understand the backend file structure before they can understand the project. The website is the map; the JSON files are the machinery beneath it.
